I'm a most of the year healthy person, so no need to be irritated by me as if I take up too much time. Never asked too much or been a pain. Once you get through reception - the doctors themselves (the ones I've had anyway) are lovely and great, but the battle at reception is enough to make you not want to get your health seen to - and just let yourself wither away from whatever makes you sick. This combined with the absolute mayhem you go through trying to make an appointment, eg; You try and make a regular appointment: "Just call in the morning." then you call in the morning and get told "Well that's not really an emergency, is it?".
Nobody WANTS to be at the doctors. They have to go. Every time I have called the reception staff have been consistently rude, dismissive and unhelpful. Every time I order my prescriptions to a local pharmacy they never arrive and I, or the pharmacist, have had to chase them up multiple times. This has often meant I go without important medication, even though I order them with plenty of time. An exception is Dr Jessica Lynas, who when I saw her was lovely - extremely understanding and receptive to my issues, listened to everything I had to say and discussed solutions in depth with me. However, I was made to feel extremely uncomfortable by one of the male GP’s I previously saw and his comments to me. He repeatedly asked me if I needed birth control and asked about my sexual activity though it was completely unrelated to my problem and denied at the beginning of the appointment. As a 19-year-old girl, this seemed very inappropriate and understandably made me uncomfortable leaving me very confused and angry. Overall a poorly run and insensitive practice which provides less than the basic standard of care and human respect and needs an extensive review. The team seems completely uninterested in addressing the root cause of any issue. My situation was that the repeat prescription system was not functioning properly, leading to my prescription being lost for three months before I could even trace its whereabouts.
Despite explaining the issue multiple times, I was assured that my medication would be ready for collection at the Buyers Road location. After numerous phone calls, I took the time  off work to visit in person—only to find out that my prescription had been sent to the pharmacy at the Practice instead.
The lack of communication, accountability, and willingness to help is truly disappointing. The reception team clearly needs a lot more training on what customer service looks like.
